narrativeReportMd:
# MedicinalProductIndication R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`MedicinalProductIndication` is not present as an R6 resource in the ballot package. Its indication use case appears to have moved into `ClinicalUseDefinition` with `type="indication"`, which is a hard instance, API, serialization, and generated-code break.

## Scope
This report compares the R4 `MedicinalProductIndication` StructureDefinition with the absent same-name R6 StructureDefinition and the inferred R6 replacement `ClinicalUseDefinition`. It covers local element changes needed to represent an indication in R6 and excludes inherited `DomainResource`, `Resource`, `Element`, and datatype-base changes.

## Main migration themes
Migration is not a rename. Implementers must create `ClinicalUseDefinition`, set the required type discriminator, supply at least one subject, move indication-specific fields under `ClinicalUseDefinition.indication`, and convert several datatypes and reference targets. The highest-risk conversions are subject references, duration, undesirable-effect references, other-therapy treatment targets, and population groups.

## Highest-impact findings
The resource identity removal is the dominant break. Additional high-impact local breaks remain even after choosing `ClinicalUseDefinition`: mandatory `type`/`subject`, moved serialized paths, `Reference` to `CodeableReference` transitions, `Quantity` duration removal, inline undesirable effects, and `Population` to `Reference(Group)`.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important where business semantics determine the mapping: old `MedicinalProduct` to `MedicinalProductDefinition`, old undesirable-effect reference graphs to inline or separate R6 clinical-use content, old inline `Population` to reusable `Group`, and R6-only status/applicability/library content when converting back to R4.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The broad merge into `ClinicalUseDefinition` is probably justified by the common clinical-use model, but several specific compatibility aids appear absent from the local inputs: a retained deprecated alias, official ConceptMap/StructureMap, and transitional choice types such as retaining `Quantity` on `duration[x]`.

## Follow-up analysis
Separate reports should cover `ClinicalUseDefinition`, `MedicinalProductDefinition`, `MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect`/R6 undesirable-effect modeling, `Population`/`Group`, and the relevant terminology value sets. Base-resource changes such as inherited language binding are intentionally out of scope here.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `MedicinalProductIndication` is removed/merged in R6; the indication use case maps to `ClinicalUseDefinition` with `type="indication"`. The top migration concerns are resource identity/API breakage, mandatory type/subject plus path moves, and datatype/reference changes for subject, duration, undesirable effects, other therapy, and population. Confidence is medium-high for the structural break, but medium overall because no official ConceptMap or narrative migration rationale was available.
summary.migrationThemesMd: The migration pattern is: create `ClinicalUseDefinition`; set `type` to `indication`; ensure a `subject`; move indication fields into `indication`; convert simple concepts to `CodeableReference.concept`; migrate old resource references to R6 definition resources; materialize populations as `Group`; and preserve R6-only status/applicability/library data with extensions or companion resources when down-converting.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the same-name R6 artifact is absent and that `ClinicalUseDefinition` is the appropriate R6 indication model, based on local StructureDefinitions, package indexes, and the R6 old-types CodeSystem. Confidence is lower for exact migration semantics because the local inputs did not include official diffs, ConceptMaps, StructureMaps, narrative ballot rationale, or terminology expansions.

findings.title: MedicinalProductIndication is absent in R6 and its indication use case moved to ClinicalUseDefinition

oldState.summary: R4 defines MedicinalProductIndication as a concrete DomainResource specialization.
oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, `MedicinalProductIndication` is a standalone resource with canonical URL `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/MedicinalProductIndication`, `kind=resource`, `type=MedicinalProductIndication`, and `abstract=false`.

newState.summary: No same-name R6 StructureDefinition exists; R6 ClinicalUseDefinition is the closest local replacement for indication content.

semanticText.definition: A single issue - either an indication, contraindication, interaction or an undesirable effect for a medicinal product, medication, device or procedure.

newState.narrativeMd: The assigned R6 path `StructureDefinition-MedicinalProductIndication.json` is absent. R6 has `ClinicalUseDefinition`, whose description and required type code system include the `indication` clinical-use category. The R6 `fhir-old-types` CodeSystem lists `MedicinalProductIndication` as an old resource name no longer used in this FHIR version.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `ClinicalUseDefinition` is the only R6 resource whose StructureDefinition explicitly covers indications and whose search parameters include `ClinicalUseDefinition-indication`. No R6 StructureDefinition or package-index entry exists for the old resource name.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct instance and API break. A JSON/XML resource with `resourceType: "MedicinalProductIndication"` is not an R6 instance of any resource in the core package, so strict R6 validators, generated parsers, REST endpoints, search parameters, and code using the old class name fail before considering child elements. R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition` instances can sometimes be mapped back to R4 indication resources, but only for the `type="indication"` subset and with losses for new fields and changed datatypes.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Indications are clinically and regulatorily meaningful. A migration that drops indication content or confuses indications with contraindications, interactions, warnings, or undesirable effects can materially affect product-use decisions.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal of consolidating related clinical-use issues into `ClinicalUseDefinition` is reasonable, and the old standalone resource family would be costly to keep forever. A less-breaking base design was possible only by retaining `MedicinalProductIndication` in parallel as a deprecated resource or alias. Because that would materially undermine the single-resource consolidation and create long-lived duplicate representations, the break is probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.inferredGoal: Consolidate clinical-use issues into one resource with a type discriminator and shared subject/status/category/logic fields.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain a deprecated `MedicinalProductIndication` base resource as a transitional parallel representation while introducing `ClinicalUseDefinition`; maps alone are migration aids, not the base alternative.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best base-design alternative would have been to keep `MedicinalProductIndication` as a deprecated R6 resource, potentially constrained to map to `ClinicalUseDefinition` indication semantics. That would preserve most R4 instances, generated classes, REST routes, and old `resourceType` dispatch. The tradeoff is significant: implementers and the specification would need to support two canonical ways to represent the same indication, and deprecated resource families often persist much longer than intended. A ConceptMap or StructureMap would help migration but is not itself a backward-compatible base resource design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old resourceType and endpoint shapes, but keeps duplicate indication resource models alive and may prolong the old medicinal-product model indefinitely.

R6 ClinicalUseDefinition covers indications and uses a required `type` discriminator.
evidence.quote: type binding includes indication | contraindication | interaction | undesirable-effect | warning

examples.examplesMd: The fragments are illustrative rather than full validated resources. The key break is the resource identity: the old `resourceType` is not an R6 resource type.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 does not carry forward `MedicinalProductIndication` as a resource. The indication semantics appear to be folded into `ClinicalUseDefinition` with `type="indication"`. This is the highest-impact change because it breaks instance identity, generated classes, REST resource names, search surfaces, and any FHIRPath or mapping logic rooted at `MedicinalProductIndication`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid `MedicinalProductIndication` instance is R6-invalid as-is because the resource type is unknown in the R6 core definitions. Conversely, only a subset of R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition` instances (`type="indication"`) are candidates for an R4 indication resource, and even those may contain fields and datatypes R4 cannot represent.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Migration should create `ClinicalUseDefinition` resources, set `type` to `indication`, convert the subject and indication-specific fields using explicit element maps, and separately handle linked undesirable effects, population groups, and optional R6 lifecycle/logic fields. Systems should add regression tests for resourceType dispatch, REST endpoint routing, search parameters, serialization, and generated model classes.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The consolidation is understandable, but it could have been made less disruptive by retaining a deprecated resource alias/profile or by publishing an authoritative ConceptMap/StructureMap from the old medicinal-product resources to `ClinicalUseDefinition`. Without that, compatibility is a migration project rather than a validator setting.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The replacement identity is inferred from local R6 definitions and terminology; no official diff or ConceptMap was present in the package inputs.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 does not define a same-name `MedicinalProductIndication` resource; the indication use case is represented by `ClinicalUseDefinition` with `type = indication`. That is a real resource identity, endpoint, parser, validator, search, and generated-class break. However, the R4 artifact was FMM 0/trial-use, and consolidating several low-maturity medicinal-product clinical-use resources into one typed resource is a coherent R6 design goal. The break is significant migration work, but the less-breaking alternative would keep a parallel deprecated resource family alive.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition defines concrete resource id/type `MedicinalProductIndication` with FMM 0 and trial-use status.
R6 package has `StructureDefinition-ClinicalUseDefinition.json` and no same-name `StructureDefinition-MedicinalProductIndication.json`.
R6 `CodeSystem-fhir-old-types` lists `MedicinalProductIndication` as an old resource name.
FHIR ClinicalUseDefinition scope page describes indications for medicines/devices/procedures and use in regulator dossiers, knowledge bases, and decision support.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 0/trial-use materially softens the stability concern, so the resource removal alone is not enough for Revisit. Regulatory and decision-support relevance keeps the migration risk real, but not disproportionate.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 instance with `resourceType: MedicinalProductIndication` is not an R6 core resource and code using the old REST/type identity must migrate.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. R6 could have retained a deprecated `MedicinalProductIndication` alias/resource for transition, but that would preserve duplicate representations and keep the old medicinal-product resource family in the base model.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly identifies a hard resource identity break and a partial deprecated-resource alternative, but the low FMM makes this an expected migration burden rather than a design issue needing renewed attention.

findings.title: R6 indication representation requires an explicit type code and at least one subject

oldState.summary: R4 has no type discriminator and `subject` is optional (`0..*`).
oldState.narrativeMd: `MedicinalProductIndication.subject` could be omitted. The resource identity itself implied that the clinical-use issue was an indication.

newState.summary: R6 ClinicalUseDefinition has mandatory `type` (`1..1`) and mandatory repeating `subject` (`1..*`), plus local invariants tying indication content to `type="indication"`.

binding.description: Overall defining type of this clinical use definition.

constraints.human: Indication, Contraindication, Interaction, UndesirableEffect and Warning cannot be used in the same instance
ClinicalUseDefinition.indication can only be used when type is 'indication'

newState.narrativeMd: A valid migrated indication needs `ClinicalUseDefinition.type = "indication"` and at least one `subject`. If the indication backbone is present, `cud-3` requires the type to match.

facts.note: New mandatory discriminator replacing the old resource identity.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `MedicinalProductIndication.subject` maps to `ClinicalUseDefinition.subject`; the old resource type maps semantically to the new required `type` code `indication`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Even after choosing the correct R6 replacement resource, an R4 instance with no `subject` can be valid in R4 but cannot satisfy the R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition.subject` minimum. A transform must also synthesize the required `type` code. Validators enforce both cardinality and the required `clinical-use-definition-type` value set; generated constructors or serializers may also require non-null fields.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: A missing or incorrectly typed subject can detach indication statements from the product or medication they are meant to govern.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The required `type` is intrinsic to the merged `ClinicalUseDefinition` design and is not meaningfully avoidable once indications, contraindications, interactions, warnings, and undesirable effects share one resource. The `subject` minimum increase is less strictly necessary, but the goal of making every clinical-use statement self-describing and indexable is reasonable. Keeping `subject` optional would preserve old stubs at the cost of weaker baseline data quality, so the break is probably justified with a partial alternative.
justification.inferredGoal: Make a merged clinical-use resource self-describing and always linked to the product, medication, device, substance, or other subject it concerns.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the required type discriminator for the merged resource, but leave `subject` optional in the base and require it through profiles or best-practice warnings.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking R6 base design could have used `type` = `indication` while keeping `subject` at `0..*`, then required a subject in implementation profiles, IGs, or best-practice invariants. That would let R4 instances with no subject migrate structurally, but it would also permit base R6 records whose clinical subject is unknown, limiting search, safety review, and downstream interpretation.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves subjectless R4 stubs, but weakens the R6 guarantee that every clinical-use definition is linked to what it governs.

evidence.detail: R4 subject cardinality is `0..*`.
R6 ClinicalUseDefinition.type is mandatory and required-bound.
R6 ClinicalUseDefinition.subject cardinality is `1..*`.
The required type code system contains `indication`.
evidence.quote: indication = A reason for giving the medication.

examples.examplesMd: The old fragment illustrates the cardinality break: R4 allowed no `subject`; R6 requires at least one subject and an explicit type.

findings.narrativeMd: The old resource name carried the indication classification implicitly and allowed an indication without a product/medication subject. The R6 replacement makes both the classification and subject explicit. That is a useful model quality improvement, but it means migration cannot be a pure rename.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance lacking `subject` becomes invalid under the inferred R6 representation. An R6 instance with `indication` populated but a non-`indication` type fails `cud-3`; an instance with multiple issue backbones fails `cud-1`. R6-to-R4 risk from this specific change is low because R4 can infer indication from the resource type and can carry subjects if present.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Populate `ClinicalUseDefinition.type` with `indication`. Audit R4 records with no subject and decide whether the subject can be inferred from surrounding resources, source files, bundles, or regulatory context. Reject, quarantine, or annotate records where the subject cannot be established reliably.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The discriminator is unavoidable once several old resources are merged. The `subject` minimum increase was more avoidable: it could have been a profile-level requirement, but the base specification appears to prefer stronger consistency for clinical-use indexing.

freshReview.narrativeMd: A migrated indication must now state the clinical-use type explicitly and include at least one subject. R4 allowed `subject` to be absent because the resource identity carried the indication category. The new minimum can invalidate subjectless R4 records, but the requirement makes the merged ClinicalUseDefinition instance self-describing and linked to the thing it governs.
keyEvidence: R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition.type` is `1..1 code` with required binding to `clinical-use-definition-type`.
R6 root invariants include `cud-3`, requiring `indication` content only when `type = indication`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0 softens the compatibility expectation for old subjectless records. The subject is nevertheless central to safe interpretation, so the break remains meaningful but proportionate.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 indication with no subject cannot satisfy R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition.subject` minimum, and a transform must synthesize `type = indication`.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. R6 could have kept `subject` optional and required it in profiles or warnings, but that would weaken the base guarantee that every clinical-use statement is tied to its medication, product, device, or other subject.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly calls out a hard cardinality break and partial alternative; I give the low-FMM context more weight and view the base requirement as proportionate.

findings.title: Indication-specific data moved from resource-level fields into ClinicalUseDefinition.indication

oldState.summary: R4 places indication details directly under MedicinalProductIndication.
oldState.narrativeMd: Fields such as `diseaseSymptomProcedure`, `diseaseStatus`, `comorbidity`, `intendedEffect`, `duration`, `otherTherapy`, and `undesirableEffect` are direct children of the R4 resource.

newState.narrativeMd: The replacement resource has separate backbones for indication, contraindication, interaction, undesirable effect, and warning. Indication details must be placed under `ClinicalUseDefinition.indication` and constrained by the root `type`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element names and definitions are closely preserved, but their parent changed from the resource root to the `indication` backbone.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Old serialized paths, generated property names, FHIRPath expressions, JSON patches, search extraction code, and mapping rules targeting `MedicinalProductIndication.<field>` no longer address valid R6 content. A syntactic migration must create the `indication` backbone and move the fields before element-specific type conversions are applied.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Moving fields without preserving their association to the indication context can lead to dropped or misplaced clinical-use qualifiers.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Moving indication-specific content under an `indication` backbone is a coherent consequence of the merged clinical-use resource. A less-breaking design could have retained top-level aliases, but that would duplicate the same facts both at the resource root and inside the issue-specific backbone. Given the validation and maintenance risk of divergent duplicate content, the break is probably justified.
justification.inferredGoal: Separate issue-specific details within a shared ClinicalUseDefinition resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep deprecated top-level aliases for indication-specific fields on `ClinicalUseDefinition` while adding the `indication` backbone.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best base-design alternative would be to accept legacy top-level fields such as `diseaseStatus` and `duration` as deprecated aliases on `ClinicalUseDefinition`, with invariants or mapping rules tying them to `ClinicalUseDefinition.indication.*`. This would preserve more R4 wire shape, but it would make clients support both old and new paths for the same semantics and could allow conflicting values unless validators imposed additional rules.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Aliases ease wire compatibility but create duplicate same-resource representations that need synchronization and may never disappear.

evidence.detail: R4 defines indication-specific elements as direct resource children.
R6 defines the corresponding indication-specific elements under `ClinicalUseDefinition.indication`.

examples.examplesMd: The example highlights the parent-path move; actual migration must also address CodeableReference and subject conversion.

findings.narrativeMd: Most local content did not merely rename the resource; it moved into an issue-specific backbone. Existing code that reads or writes top-level R4 indication properties will miss the R6 data unless it is updated to navigate through `ClinicalUseDefinition.indication`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Raw R4 property placement is invalid in R6. R6 indication content can be structurally moved back to R4 for fields with compatible datatypes, but fields with new datatypes, references, or repeat counts need additional logic covered by other findings.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Implement a two-stage transform: first change resource identity and create the `indication` backbone; then apply field-specific type conversions for subject, duration, undesirable effects, other therapy, population, and CodeableReference fields. Update generated-code mappings and FHIRPath expressions.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The move is a predictable consequence of a merged model. Backward-compatible aliases would have reduced wire breakage but would require duplicate fields or custom compatibility extensions.

freshReview.narrativeMd: Indication detail fields moved from the resource root to `ClinicalUseDefinition.indication`. Existing FHIRPath, JSON Patch, serializers, DTOs, and generated properties that expect root-level R4 fields must be updated. This is a real wire-shape and codegen break, but it is a direct consequence of using one shared resource for indication, contraindication, interaction, undesirable effect, and warning content.
keyEvidence: R4 defines `diseaseSymptomProcedure`, `diseaseStatus`, `comorbidity`, `intendedEffect`, `duration`, `otherTherapy`, and `undesirableEffect` as direct children of `MedicinalProductIndication`.
R6 defines the corresponding indication-specific elements under `ClinicalUseDefinition.indication`.
R6 root invariants separate the issue backbones by `ClinicalUseDefinition.type`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0 softens the burden to preserve old root paths. Because the move is model-wide but mechanically understandable, the low maturity supports treating it as acceptable migration work.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: old generated properties and path expressions no longer point at valid R6 content; raw old top-level fields are not valid under the R6 replacement.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. Deprecated top-level aliases could preserve more R4 wire shape, but they would duplicate the same facts inside and outside `indication` and require conflict rules.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly finds a high path/codegen break, but the merged-resource design gives a strong reason for the move.

findings.title: subject changed from Reference(MedicinalProduct|Medication) to mandatory CodeableReference with different target set

oldState.summary: Optional repeating Reference to MedicinalProduct or Medication.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 subject values were references only, with target profiles limited to `MedicinalProduct` and `Medication`.

newState.summary: Mandatory repeating CodeableReference to a broader but changed set of targets, with example medication-code binding.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 allows either a concept or a reference via `CodeableReference`, and the old `MedicinalProduct` target is replaced by `MedicinalProductDefinition`. Several non-medicinal subjects are now allowed.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Both elements identify the medication/product/etc. for which the indication applies.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 `Medication` references can be wrapped in `CodeableReference.reference`, but R4 `MedicinalProduct` references target a resource type that is not the R6 subject target; they need migration to `MedicinalProductDefinition` or another R6 resource. R6 subjects can be code-only or refer to devices, plans, activities, nutrition products, biologically derived products, or substances that have no direct R4 `MedicinalProductIndication.subject` target.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect subject migration can associate an indication with the wrong product class or lose the subject entirely.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of making clinical-use subjects cover products, medications, devices, substances, procedures, and coded concepts is reasonable. R4 `Medication` references can be wrapped, but R4 `MedicinalProduct` references depend on a resource model that is no longer current. A less-breaking base design exists only partially because preserving old targets would either retain the old medicinal-product resource family or require mixed representations with material validation and implementation costs.
justification.inferredGoal: Allow clinical-use definitions to apply to coded concepts and to a broader set of product, device, procedure, substance, and plan resources.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Allow the old `Reference(MedicinalProduct|Medication)` form or old target as a transitional base option alongside the new `CodeableReference` subject.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A base-compatible design could have allowed a legacy `Reference(MedicinalProduct|Medication)` subject, or at least retained `MedicinalProduct` as an allowed target while adding the broader R6 `CodeableReference` target list. That would preserve more R4 instances than a migration-only map. The cost is that R6 consumers would need to support obsolete and current product models, plus concept-only `CodeableReference` subjects, in one element.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve more R4 subjects, but carries forward removed target models and forces clients to handle old/new reference and CodeableReference variants.

evidence.detail: R4 subject is Reference to MedicinalProduct or Medication.
R6 subject is CodeableReference with a broader target list.
R6 subject is mandatory.

examples.examplesMd: Old `Medication` references can usually be wrapped directly. Old `MedicinalProduct` references require a separate migration to the R6 medicinal-product definition resource.

findings.narrativeMd: `subject` is no longer a simple optional reference to R4 `MedicinalProduct` or `Medication`. It is mandatory and uses `CodeableReference`, which changes generated types and allows concept-only subjects. The old `MedicinalProduct` resource target is not accepted in the R6 definition.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances using `Reference(MedicinalProduct)` are not valid R6 subjects without target migration. R6 code-only or non-medication subjects cannot be losslessly represented in R4 because R4 requires a reference to `MedicinalProduct` or `Medication` for this element.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Build or reuse a cross-version map from R4 `MedicinalProduct` to R6 `MedicinalProductDefinition`. Wrap retained `Medication` references as `CodeableReference.reference`. Decide how to handle R6 code-only subjects when back-porting: use an extension, create a referenceable R4 resource where possible, or flag for manual review.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Keeping the old target alongside new targets would have been the most compatible for R4 data but inconsistent with removal of the old medicinal-product resource family. The main missing compatibility aid is an authoritative cross-version map.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `subject` changed from an optional `Reference(MedicinalProduct|Medication)` to mandatory `CodeableReference` with a broader R6 target set. R4 `Medication` references can usually be wrapped, but R4 `MedicinalProduct` references need a separate migration to `MedicinalProductDefinition` or another allowed R6 subject. The path is central and safety-relevant, but retaining old resource targets would undercut the larger R6 medicinal-product redesign.
keyEvidence: R6 `subject` minimum is 1, while R4 `subject` minimum is 0.
R6 package index includes `MedicinalProductDefinition` and does not include current `MedicinalProduct` or `MedicinalProductIndication` StructureDefinitions.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0 reduces the expectation that old references remain valid. The domain still matters because the subject determines which product or treatment the indication applies to.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 references to `MedicinalProduct` are not valid R6 subject targets without target-resource migration; R6 code-only or newly targeted subjects also lose information when mapped back to R4.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. R6 could have allowed legacy `Reference(MedicinalProduct|Medication)` or retained `MedicinalProduct` as a target, but that would force clients to support obsolete and current product models in one element.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly identifies high migration and reverse-representation risk; I view the target change as proportionate given the broader low-maturity product model replacement.

findings.title: Clinical descriptor fields changed from CodeableConcept to CodeableReference with new bindings and intendedEffect repeatability

oldState.summary: R4 uses CodeableConcept for disease/symptom/procedure, disease status, comorbidity, and intended effect; intendedEffect is `0..1`.
oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 descriptor fields are coded/text concepts only and have no local terminology bindings in the base StructureDefinition.

newState.summary: R6 uses CodeableReference(ObservationDefinition) for these fields, adds example/preferred bindings, and changes intendedEffect to `0..*`.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 values may be inline concepts or references to `ObservationDefinition`. `intendedEffect` can repeat and has a preferred product-intended-use binding.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Element names and clinical definitions are preserved under the R6 indication backbone, with changed value representation.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 concepts can generally be represented as `CodeableReference.concept`, so this is not a hard R4-to-R6 data-loss break by itself. It is still a runtime/codegen break because generated property types change. R6 references to `ObservationDefinition` and repeated `intendedEffect` values are not directly representable in R4, which only has CodeableConcept and at most one intended effect.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Descriptor conversion determines the exact disease, disease status, comorbidity, or treatment aim attached to the indication.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of allowing descriptors to be either coded concepts or references to reusable observation definitions is reasonable, and `CodeableReference` is the clean unified R6 representation. A less-breaking design could have kept the old `CodeableConcept` fields and added reference companions, but that would create parallel ways to state the same disease, status, comorbidity, or intended effect. The material ambiguity makes the existing break probably justified.
justification.inferredGoal: Permit clinical-use descriptors to be either coded concepts or references to reusable ObservationDefinition resources, with more terminology guidance.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the R4 `CodeableConcept` descriptor fields and add optional reference-valued companions for `ObservationDefinition` instead of replacing them with `CodeableReference`.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best alternative would preserve fields such as `diseaseSymptomProcedure` as direct `CodeableConcept` values and add optional references such as a companion observation-definition element. That would keep R4 payloads valid for common coded cases while still enabling richer reusable definitions. The tradeoff is duplicate representation: implementations would need rules for whether the concept, the reference, or both are authoritative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves simple R4 coded values, but splits one descriptor across concept/reference representations and complicates validation and client handling.

evidence.detail: R4 descriptor fields are CodeableConcept.
R4 intendedEffect is single-valued.
R6 diseaseSymptomProcedure is CodeableReference to ObservationDefinition.
R6 intendedEffect repeats and has a preferred binding.

examples.examplesMd: A simple R4 CodeableConcept maps naturally to `concept`; R6 reference-valued or repeated values require extensions, resource materialization, or manual reduction when converting back to R4.

findings.narrativeMd: Several clinical descriptors keep their clinical role but change from `CodeableConcept` to `CodeableReference`. This is migration-friendly for simple coded values but not transparent to generated code, JSON shape, or R6-to-R4 conversion.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 coded values can remain valid after wrapping into `CodeableReference.concept`; no R6 required binding makes the old codes invalid by itself. R6 reference-valued descriptors and multiple intended effects cannot be represented in the base R4 element shapes without losing information.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map each R4 CodeableConcept into the `concept` arm of the R6 CodeableReference. For R6-to-R4, if a descriptor has a reference, decide whether to dereference it into a concept, create an extension, or reject the down-conversion. Test multiple intended effects explicitly.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is probably justified by the general R6 move toward CodeableReference for coded-or-referenced clinical definitions. A backward-compatible alternative would have kept old concept fields and added optional reference companions, but that would be a more awkward model.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Terminology expansion was not performed; binding impact is based on binding strength and declared value-set URLs only.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The disease/status/comorbidity/intended-effect descriptors changed from `CodeableConcept` to `CodeableReference(ObservationDefinition)`, and `intendedEffect` became repeatable. Simple R4 coded values can be carried in the `concept` arm, so this is not a severe forward data-loss break, but it changes the JSON shape and generated model type and creates reverse loss for reference-valued or repeated R6 descriptors.
keyEvidence: R6 disease/status/comorbidity bindings are example-strength, not required.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0 softens concern about generated-type churn. The affected descriptors are clinically meaningful, but forward migration for ordinary coded values is mostly mechanical.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: old CodeableConcept-valued properties must be wrapped as `CodeableReference.concept`, and generated code changes from concept fields to CodeableReference fields.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. R6 could have kept direct CodeableConcept fields and added reference companions, but that would split one clinical descriptor across two representations and require precedence rules.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report appropriately treats this as lower than the hard target/type removals; I agree the alternative has real duplicate-representation costs.

findings.title: duration changed from Quantity to duration[x] with Range or string, removing direct Quantity representation

newState.summary: R6 duration is optional choice `duration[x]` with Range or string (`0..1`).
newState.narrativeMd: `ClinicalUseDefinition.indication.duration[x]` allows `durationRange` or `durationString`; it does not list `Quantity` as a choice type.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The short/definition text in both versions describes timing or duration information for the indication.

impact.impactRationaleMd: A direct R4 `Quantity` payload cannot be copied into any R6 `duration[x]` choice. A transform must choose whether a single quantity should become a textual duration or a Range, and that decision can affect semantics. Generated models also change from one concrete type to a choice type.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Duration qualifiers can materially narrow an indication, such as treatment within a time window after an event.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of supporting ranges and narrative duration text is reasonable, but the supplied definitions do not show why the existing `Quantity` form had to be removed. Because R6 already uses a choice element for duration, retaining `Quantity` would have met the goal with a modest long-term cost. This specific type removal therefore looks probably avoidable.
justification.inferredGoal: Represent timing/duration text and ranges such as “from a few days until less than 35 days”.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add `Quantity` as a third `duration[x]` choice alongside `Range` and `string`.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A backward-compatible base design would define `ClinicalUseDefinition.indication.duration[x]` as `Range | string | Quantity`. Existing R4 exact durations could migrate without reinterpretation, while R6 could still represent ranges and textual windows. The main tradeoff is a broader choice domain and slightly more consumer logic, not a fundamental model conflict.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Adds one choice type for consumers to handle, but preserves exact R4 durations losslessly while still supporting new range and text forms.

evidence.detail: R4 duration type is Quantity.
R6 duration choices are Range and string.

examples.examplesMd: Mapping a single Quantity to a Range with identical low/high is one possible convention, but the base definitions do not prescribe it.

findings.narrativeMd: `duration` is a concrete example where the R6 replacement does not merely wrap the old data. The old `Quantity` type disappeared, and the new element is a choice between `Range` and `string`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 quantity is invalid if copied directly into R6. R6 strings cannot be represented in R4 `Quantity` without interpretation, and R6 ranges may need reduction to a single quantity or extension when back-ported.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Define a project-level convention for quantities: either convert exact quantities to `durationRange` with equal low/high, convert to `durationString`, or use an extension when exact quantity semantics must be preserved. Include unit-normalization and boundary tests.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Because R6 already chose a choice element, retaining `Quantity` as an additional choice would have been the least disruptive path. Without narrative rationale, this specific type removal looks probably avoidable.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `duration` was a `Quantity`; R6 `indication.duration[x]` allows `Range` or `string` but not `Quantity`. A single exact duration such as six weeks therefore needs reinterpretation as a range or text. Because R6 already uses a choice element, retaining `Quantity` as an additional choice looks like a modest, direct way to preserve exact R4 data while still supporting the new range/text use cases.
keyEvidence: No local R6 evidence checked explains why exact `Quantity` duration could not remain as another choice.
Duration qualifiers can affect when or for how long an indication applies.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0 softens expected prevalence, but the change is localized, clinically meaningful, and has an apparent low-cost base-compatible design.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 Quantity duration cannot be copied into the R6 duration choice without choosing a lossy or convention-dependent representation.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Yes. Define `ClinicalUseDefinition.indication.duration[x]` as `Range | string | Quantity`; the tradeoff is one additional choice type for clients, which seems modest compared with preserving exact R4 durations.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report's high impact and less-breaking alternative assessment are persuasive even after applying the low-FMM caution.

findings.title: undesirableEffect changed from Reference(MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect) to inline ClinicalUseDefinition undesirable-effect content

oldState.summary: R4 undesirableEffect is a repeating Reference to MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 indications can link to separate undesirable-effect resources.

newState.summary: R6 indication.undesirableEffect is repeating inline content by contentReference to ClinicalUseDefinition.undesirableEffect.
newState.narrativeMd: `ClinicalUseDefinition.indication.undesirableEffect` uses `contentReference="#ClinicalUseDefinition.undesirableEffect"`, so the effect details are inline backbone content, not a reference to another resource.

facts.newValue: MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect is listed in R6 fhir-old-types, not as a current R6 StructureDefinition

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Both elements describe unwanted effects associated with the indication, but the representation changed from external resource reference to inline backbone content.

impact.impactRationaleMd: A reference such as `MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect/123` cannot be copied into the R6 indication undesirableEffect element because that element is not a Reference and the target resource family is no longer current. Migration must denormalize or separately convert the referenced resource. R6 inline effects may not have stable standalone identities for R4 back-conversion.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Undesirable effects are patient-safety-relevant; dropping or duplicating them during denormalization can misstate product risk.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Modeling undesirable effects in the shared clinical-use framework is reasonable, and inline effect content can simplify indication-local details. However, the local inputs do not explain why the old linked-resource pattern had to disappear entirely. A reference option would be a serious but partial base alternative, so the level of breakage is not clearly justified.
justification.inferredGoal: Model unwanted effects within the same clinical-use definition framework and allow indication-specific effect details.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Support a reference-valued association to a separate undesirable-effect resource or `ClinicalUseDefinition` issue in addition to inline undesirable-effect content.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could allow `ClinicalUseDefinition.indication.undesirableEffect` to be either inline content or a reference to a separate undesirable-effect `ClinicalUseDefinition` or retained legacy undesirable-effect resource. This would better preserve R4 graphs where effects are reusable master data. The cost is material: validators would need to ensure the target really represents an undesirable effect, and clients would need to reconcile linked and embedded forms.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves reusable linked effect patterns, but requires type constraints and creates linked-versus-embedded representation ambiguity.

evidence.detail: R4 undesirableEffect is a Reference to MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect.
R6 indication undesirableEffect is a contentReference to inline undesirableEffect backbone.
R6 also lists MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect as an old type.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example assumes the referenced undesirable-effect resource was resolved and summarized inline; the definitions do not supply an automatic dereference rule.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 kept undesirable effects as references to separate resources. R6 indication-specific undesirable effects are inline backbones. This changes both data normalization and identity: a reference graph must become embedded content, unless an implementation uses extensions or separate ClinicalUseDefinition resources outside this specific element.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old Reference-valued content is invalid in the R6 inline element. R6 inline content can be partly converted to a new R4 `MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect` resource, but that requires minting resource ids and deciding how to preserve links and repeated occurrences.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Resolve each R4 undesirable-effect reference during migration. Convert the target resource to R6 undesirable-effect content or to separate `ClinicalUseDefinition` records according to a documented policy, and preserve provenance/identity with identifiers or extensions when clinical reuse matters.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible path could have allowed references to `ClinicalUseDefinition` undesirable-effect resources in addition to inline content. That would preserve old graph structure but require validators and clients to support both linked and embedded patterns.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The best migration depends on how R4 installations used MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect resources: reusable master data versus indication-local details.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 linked indications to separate `MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect` resources. R6 makes `indication.undesirableEffect` inline content via a contentReference to the ClinicalUseDefinition undesirable-effect backbone. That forces dereferencing, denormalization, and possible loss of separate effect identity or reuse. Because undesirable effects are safety-relevant and the linked-versus-inline choice is semantically important, this path deserves renewed design attention despite the old artifact's low maturity.
keyEvidence: R6 `fhir-old-types` lists `MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect` as an old resource name.
ClinicalUseDefinition scope describes undesirable effects as potential negative outcomes, distinct from actual AdverseEvent records.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0 lowers the assumption of broad installed base, but safety relevance and lossy graph-to-inline migration are strong enough to keep this concerning.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: a Reference to a standalone undesirable-effect resource is not valid in the R6 inline element; R6-to-R4 conversion may also require minting resource identities.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. R6 could allow a reference to a separate undesirable-effect ClinicalUseDefinition, or a transitional legacy reference, in addition to inline content. The tradeoff is linked-versus-embedded ambiguity and validators needing to prove the target has the right issue type.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report identifies the right high-risk migration mechanism and partial alternative; my final judgment emphasizes that the lossy safety-relevant representation change merits Revisit.

findings.title: otherTherapy child elements were renamed and the therapy target changed to CodeableReference

oldState.summary: R4 otherTherapy has mandatory `therapyRelationshipType` and mandatory `medication[x]` (CodeableConcept or Reference to MedicinalProduct, Medication, Substance, or SubstanceSpecification).
oldState.narrativeMd: The nested backbone is optional and repeating, but once present both child fields are required.

newState.summary: R6 otherTherapy has mandatory `relationshipType` and mandatory `treatment` as CodeableReference to a revised target set, with preferred/example bindings.
newState.narrativeMd: The old `therapyRelationshipType` name is shortened to `relationshipType`; `medication[x]` becomes the more general `treatment` CodeableReference.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The parent and child definitions are near-identical in purpose, but R6 uses broader names and the R6 medicinal-product/substance definitions.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Existing R4 JSON uses `therapyRelationshipType` and `medicationCodeableConcept`/`medicationReference`; those names are not valid under the R6 otherTherapy backbone. References to old medicinal-product or substance resource types also require target migration. R6 therapies that are nutrition products, biologically derived products, activities, or code-only treatments cannot map directly to the old R4 target domain.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Other-therapy relationships can constrain when an indication applies, for example adjunctive or replacement therapy use.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Generalizing other-therapy content to treatments and current R6 product/substance resources is a reasonable goal. Still, the naming break itself appears only partly necessary: R6 could have lived with the older names plus clearer definitions and broader target support. Because old target resources and `CodeableReference` unification create real tradeoffs, the alternative is partial, but the extra rename break is not clearly justified by the local evidence.
justification.inferredGoal: Generalize other-therapy representation and align targets with current R6 product/substance resources.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain R4 child names such as `therapyRelationshipType` and `medication[x]` with broader definitions or transitional aliases while adding current R6 target support.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could keep `therapyRelationshipType` and `medication[x]` as deprecated or broadened fields, accepting the old `CodeableConcept` and `Reference` wire forms while adding current R6 targets or companion fields for broader treatments. This would preserve common R4 instances. The downside is a nonoptimal medication-focused name for therapies that may be substances, nutrition products, biologically derived products, or activities, plus continued handling of old target-resource families.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves much of the old wire shape, but leaves medication-centric naming for non-medication treatments and does not fully solve old target-resource migrations.

evidence.detail: R4 relationship child is named therapyRelationshipType and is mandatory.
R4 therapy item is medication[x] with CodeableConcept or Reference choices.
R6 relationship child is named relationshipType and is mandatory.
R6 therapy item is treatment and uses CodeableReference.

examples.examplesMd: The old child names must be changed, and some references require migration to R6 definition resources.

findings.narrativeMd: `otherTherapy` survives but its children are not wire-compatible. The old medication-focused choice becomes a generalized treatment CodeableReference, and several old targets are replaced by R6 definition resources.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old child names and old target references fail R6 validation after resource migration. R6 code-only or newly targeted treatments require extensions or manual reduction when represented in R4.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Rename `therapyRelationshipType` to `relationshipType`. Convert `medicationCodeableConcept` to `treatment.concept` and `medicationReference` to `treatment.reference` after target-resource migration. Pay special attention to R4 `Substance` and `SubstanceSpecification` references.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is consistent with the broader R6 resource redesign. A less-breaking alternative would have kept `medication[x]` as an alias for `treatment`, but that would preserve a medication-centric name for non-medication therapies.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `otherTherapy` remains conceptually present, but its child names and treatment representation changed: `therapyRelationshipType` becomes `relationshipType`, and `medication[x]` becomes a broader `treatment` CodeableReference with current R6 target resources. This breaks old wire names and some old reference targets, yet the broader treatment terminology is a reasonable cleanup for low-maturity content that already included non-medication targets.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0 softens the stability concern for the rename and target modernization. The field can affect clinical context, but the migration is generally mechanical when target-resource maps exist.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 child names such as `therapyRelationshipType` and `medicationReference` are not valid R6 names, and legacy product/substance targets need migration.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. R6 could have kept deprecated aliases for the old child names or retained `medication[x]`, but that would preserve medication-centric naming for broader treatments and duplicate the new `treatment` representation.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly notes a high wire-shape break, but I find the R6 naming and target changes proportionate under low FMM.

findings.title: population changed from inline Population datatype to Reference(Group)

oldState.summary: R4 population is a repeating inline Population datatype.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 carries the applicable population group directly as `Population` datatype content on the indication resource.

newState.summary: R6 population is a repeating Reference to Group.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 points to `Group` resources for population applicability rather than embedding the old `Population` datatype.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Both elements have the same short definition: the population group to which the clinical use applies.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Inline R4 `Population` data cannot be copied into an R6 Reference. Migration must materialize or identify a `Group` resource and preserve the original population criteria. R6 references to Groups cannot be represented in R4 without embedding or summarizing the group criteria into Population or using an extension.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Population restrictions can determine whether an indication applies to pediatric, adult, pregnant, genotype-specific, or other subgroups.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Reusing `Group` for applicable populations is a reasonable R6 direction, especially when populations are shared across clinical-use definitions. The supplied definitions do not show why inline `Population` could not remain as a base option during transition. Because supporting both inline and referenced populations would add material ambiguity and implementation burden, the alternative is partial, but the hard replacement is not clearly justified.
justification.inferredGoal: Represent applicable populations using reusable Group resources.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain inline `Population` values and add `Reference(Group)` as a transition or companion representation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could keep `ClinicalUseDefinition.population` able to carry inline `Population` content or add a companion inline population element while also allowing `Reference(Group)`. That would preserve R4 population criteria without immediate resource materialization. The tradeoff is duplicate modeling: clients would need to understand when a Group reference supersedes, duplicates, or complements inline criteria.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves inline R4 population criteria, but creates two population representations and requires reconciliation rules between inline data and reusable Groups.

evidence.detail: R4 population type is Population.
R6 population type is Reference(Group).

examples.examplesMd: The example assumes the old Population criteria have been converted into or associated with a Group resource.

findings.narrativeMd: Population applicability changed from embedded criteria to references. This affects validation and persistence: migration must either create Groups or map to existing Groups, not just rename a property.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old inline Population objects are invalid at the R6 path. R6 Group references are not cleanly representable in R4 unless the Group can be summarized into the old Population datatype or carried by extension/reference outside the base element.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Design a Group materialization strategy before bulk migration. Preserve identifiers and provenance so multiple indications can share a population definition when appropriate. Validate that converted Groups capture age, gender, race, physiologic condition, and other criteria formerly represented by Population.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A compatibility choice of `Population | Reference(Group)` would have reduced immediate breakage. The R6-only Group reference is cleaner for reuse but raises the migration bar.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The detailed Population-to-Group mapping should be reviewed with the reports for the `Population` datatype and `Group` resource.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 embedded applicable population criteria using the `Population` datatype. R6 instead points to `Group` resources. That is not a simple wrapper change: migration must either find or create Groups and preserve criteria such as age range or other subgroup definitions. Population limits can determine whether an indication is applicable, so a choice that forces resource materialization and can lose inline criteria deserves renewed review.
keyEvidence: R6 package index includes `StructureDefinition-Group.json`; the inspected ClinicalUseDefinition element does not allow inline Population.
ClinicalUseDefinition scope includes use in decision support and regulatory/product knowledge contexts where applicability populations can be material.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0 softens expected installed-base impact, but population applicability is central enough and the migration is expert-dependent enough that the low maturity does not eliminate concern.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: inline R4 Population objects cannot be used where R6 requires a Reference(Group), and R6-to-R4 conversion may lose Group identity or detailed criteria.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. A `population[x]` choice allowing `Population` or `Reference(Group)` would preserve more R4 instances while enabling reusable Groups. The tradeoff is carrying an old draft datatype forward and requiring rules when inline and referenced populations disagree.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly flags high migration and partial alternative; I classify it as Revisit because the path can be safety/applicability critical and the base choice alternative is plausible.

findings.title: R6 replacement adds optional identifier/category/status/applicability/library fields, including modifier status, with no R4 base slots

oldState.summary: R4 MedicinalProductIndication has no local identifier, category, status, applicability expression, or library elements.
oldState.narrativeMd: Any equivalent business identifiers, lifecycle status, categorization, or computable applicability logic would need extensions or external context in R4.

newState.summary: R6 ClinicalUseDefinition adds optional identifiers, categories, lifecycle status, applicability expression, and logic libraries; `status` is a modifier element.
newState.narrativeMd: `ClinicalUseDefinition.status` is `0..1 CodeableConcept`, preferred-bound to publication-status, and `isModifier=true`; `indication.applicability` is an Expression; `library` is canonical(Library).

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: These are local elements in the replacement resource with no corresponding local element in R4 MedicinalProductIndication.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Optional additions do not make old R4 instances invalid when migrating forward. They do create R6-to-R4 representability and runtime risks: `status` is a modifier that changes interpretability, while applicability expressions and libraries can encode computable conditions that R4 has no base element to carry.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Ignoring retired/draft/current status or computable applicability logic could cause systems to apply an indication outside its intended context.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding optional identifier, category, status, applicability, and library fields is a reasonable R6 enhancement and does not make R4 instances invalid when migrating forward. The modifier nature of `status` raises safety concerns for R6-to-R4 loss, but that is not evidence of avoidable R4-to-R6 breakage.
justification.inferredGoal: Add management metadata and computable applicability logic to clinical-use definitions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking base alternative is applicable because these are optional R6 additions, not an R4-to-R6 breaking requirement.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because the added fields are optional, preserving R4-valid instances does not require an alternative base design. R4 systems that need round-trip support can use extensions or companion resources for down-conversion, but those are migration/backport mitigations rather than a less-breaking R6 base model.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 round trips still need extensions or policy, but that is a down-conversion mitigation rather than a backward-compatible base-design alternative.

evidence.detail: R6 adds business identifiers.
R6 adds status as a modifier element.
R6 adds an applicability Expression.
R6 adds canonical references to Library.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 fragment is structurally meaningful but has no base R4 fields for status/applicability/library. Extensions or out-of-band policy are needed for down-conversion.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds useful metadata and logic fields around the indication model. These are not R4-to-R6 breaking additions, but they matter for round-trip conversion and client behavior because at least one (`status`) is modifier information.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old R4 instances remain migratable without these fields. R6 instances using them cannot be faithfully represented in base R4 `MedicinalProductIndication`; dropping a modifier `status` or applicability expression can change meaning even though no validator error would occur after loss.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6-to-R4 transforms, preserve these fields in extensions or a companion Provenance/Basic/Library strategy, and block silent down-conversion if `status` or applicability materially changes use. R6 clients should treat `status` as modifier information during decision support.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Because these are optional additions, adding them directly to R6 is a reasonable design. The backward-compatible gap is primarily lack of an official R4 extension map for systems that need round trips.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The added R6 fields (`identifier`, `category`, `status`, `indication.applicability`, and `library`) are optional. They do not make an R4 indication harder to migrate forward. `status` being a modifier and applicability/library being computable content are important for R6-to-R4 round trips, but that is a down-conversion concern rather than an R4-to-R6 breaking base design problem.
keyEvidence: R4 MedicinalProductIndication has no local identifier/category/status/applicability/library slots.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0 further reduces concern because these are optional additions. The modifier flag matters for R6 consumers, but it does not create a forward compatibility break for R4 data.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 instances using status, applicability, or library cannot be faithfully represented in base R4, but no old R4-valid instance is rejected because these fields were added.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Not applicable. Optional R6 additions are already the compatibility-preserving form for forward migration; R4 extensions may help round trips but are not a less-breaking R6 base design.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree: the existing report's round-trip caution is useful, but treating optional additions as a material R4-to-R6 break overstates this finding.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: No local fixed, pattern, or default values were identified on the R4 indication elements or their R6 indication counterparts.
No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex constraints were identified for the mapped indication elements.
No local slicing changes were found on the mapped indication content. The structural change is backbone movement and type replacement, not slicing.

Mapped core indication elements remain summary elements in R6. New optional R6 fields have their own summary flags, but those are covered as added content rather than a flag change on an existing R4 element.

Existing mapped indication-detail elements remain non-modifier. R6 adds local `ClinicalUseDefinition.status` with `isModifier=true`, which is covered as a finding. Inherited modifierExtension behavior is out of scope.
No local `mustSupport=true` requirements were identified in the R6 ClinicalUseDefinition elements inspected; R4 also did not impose local must-support requirements in the core StructureDefinition.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 replacement broadens scope beyond medicinal-product indications
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The broader scope is not itself an R4-to-R6 validation break for indication data once the correct `type="indication"` subset is used.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Implementers should avoid accidentally mapping R6 contraindications, interactions, undesirable effects, or warnings into R4 `MedicinalProductIndication` merely because they share the same replacement resource.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds example/preferred terminology bindings to several indication fields
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Except for the required `ClinicalUseDefinition.type` discriminator covered in findings, the inspected descriptor and therapy bindings are example or preferred, so they do not normally invalidate old codes at base validation time.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Terminology-aware systems may want to normalize disease, status, intended-use, relationship, and therapy codes to the new value-set guidance during migration.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: intendedEffect cardinality widens from one value to repeating
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: A maximum-cardinality increase is not a forward validation break for R4 instances with zero or one intended effect.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R6 instances with multiple intended effects need a down-conversion policy for R4, such as selecting one value, using extensions, or rejecting lossy conversion.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: This is the inferred R6 replacement resource and should have its own full R4/R6 assessment, especially for shared clinical-use issue semantics.
